Incident leadership requires a structured approach to command, communication, and mitigation under high-pressure scenarios.","type":"paragraph","text":"When critical infrastructure fails, technical expertise alone is insufficient to resolve the issue efficiently. Incident leadership requires a structured approach to command, communication, and mitigation under high-pressure scenarios."},{"order":4,"subheading":"The Incident Command System (ICS)","type":"heading","text":"The Incident Command System (ICS)"},{"order":5,"paragraph":"Adapted from emergency services, the Incident Command System defines clear roles to prevent chaos during a system outage or security breach. The core roles include:","type":"paragraph","text":"Adapted from emergency services, the Incident Command System defines clear roles to prevent chaos during a system outage or security breach. The core roles include:"},{"order":6,"bullet_point":"Incident Commander (IC): Has ultimate authority over the incident response strategy and resource allocation. Does not write code or debug directly.","type":"bullet_point","text":"Incident Commander (IC): Has ultimate authority over the incident response strategy and resource allocation. Does not write code or debug directly."},{"order":7,"bullet_point":"Operations Lead: Directs the technical mitigation steps and coordinates engineers actively working on the fix.","type":"bullet_point","text":"Operations Lead: Directs the technical mitigation steps and coordinates engineers actively working on the fix."},{"order":8,"bullet_point":"Communications Lead: Manages internal status updates, stakeholder notifications, and external-facing messaging.","type":"bullet_point","text":"Communications Lead: Manages internal status updates, stakeholder notifications, and external-facing messaging."},{"order":9,"subheading":"Establishing Communication Protocols","type":"heading","text":"Establishing Communication Protocols"},{"order":10,"paragraph":"During an incident, cognitive load is extremely high. Communication must be concise, predictable, and routed through dedicated channels to avoid fragmented discussions.","type":"paragraph","text":"During an incident, cognitive load is extremely high. Focus on systemic failures rather than human error."},{"order":14,"bullet_point":"Timeline Reconstruction: Document exact timestamps of detection, triage, mitigation, and resolution.","type":"bullet_point","text":"Timeline Reconstruction: Document exact timestamps of detection, triage, mitigation, and resolution."},{"order":15,"bullet_point":"Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Use the \"Five Whys\" technique to trace failures back to foundational architectural or process gaps.","type":"bullet_point","text":"Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Use the \"Five Whys\" technique to trace failures back to foundational architectural or process gaps."},{"order":16,"bullet_point":"Action Items: Assign clear owners and deadlines for preventive measures to ensure the same incident does not repeat.","type":"bullet_point","text":"Action Items: Assign clear owners and deadlines for preventive measures to ensure the same incident does not repeat."}]
